level1.text: A $0.050\,\text{kg}$ piece of ice at $0\,{}^\circ\text{C}$ is dropped into a fruit drink. The ice melts completely into water at $0\,{}^\circ\text{C}$. How much heat does the ice take in as it melts? Give the answer in kilojoules.

A freezer contains $0.25\,\text{kg}$ of water at $0\,{}^\circ\text{C}$. The water freezes completely into ice at $0\,{}^\circ\text{C}$. How much heat does the water give out as it freezes? Give the answer in kilojoules.

Ice taken from the freezer is added to water in an insulated container. The bars of the graph show three quantities of heat for this mixture: the heat the water can give out as it cools to $0\,{}^\circ\text{C}$, the heat needed to warm the ice to $0\,{}^\circ\text{C}$, and the heat that melting all the ice would need. No heat is transferred to the container or the surroundings. First work out from the graph whether all the ice melts. How many grams of ice melt before thermal equilibrium? Give the answer in grams.

Ice at $0\,{}^\circ\text{C}$ is melted with a heater that transfers $60\,\text{kJ}$ of heat to the ice. How many grams of ice have time to melt, when all the heat is used for melting? Give the answer in grams.

A $0.20\,\text{kg}$ bag of ice at $-12\,{}^\circ\text{C}$ is taken from the freezer. How much heat must be transferred to the ice for its temperature to rise to $0\,{}^\circ\text{C}$ without the ice yet starting to melt? Give the answer in kilojoules.

level2.text: A calorimeter contains $0.35\,\text{kg}$ of water at $30\,{}^\circ\text{C}$. $0.060\,\text{kg}$ of ice at $0\,{}^\circ\text{C}$ is dropped into the water. What is the temperature of the contents of the calorimeter when thermal equilibrium has been reached and all the ice has melted? Assume that no heat is transferred to the calorimeter or the surroundings.

Ice at $0\,{}^\circ\text{C}$ taken from the fridge is used to cool $0.30\,\text{kg}$ of water from $18\,{}^\circ\text{C}$ to $0\,{}^\circ\text{C}$. How many grams of ice must melt? Assume that no heat is transferred to the surroundings. Give the answer in grams.

Ice of mass $0.40\,\text{kg}$ and temperature $-10\,{}^\circ\text{C}$ is heated with an $800\,\text{W}$ heater until all the ice has melted into water at $0\,{}^\circ\text{C}$. Assume that all the power of the heater is transferred to the ice. How long does the heating take? Give the answer in seconds.

The latent heat of fusion of ice is measured with a calorimeter. The calorimeter contains $0.200\,\text{kg}$ of water at $30.0\,{}^\circ\text{C}$. $0.0500\,\text{kg}$ of ice at $0\,{}^\circ\text{C}$ is dropped into the water. When the ice has melted completely, the measured temperature is $8.1\,{}^\circ\text{C}$. Determine the specific latent heat of fusion of ice. The heat capacity of the calorimeter itself and heat losses are ignored. Give the answer in kJ/kg.

level3.text: A thermos jug contains $0.600\,\text{kg}$ of water at $35.0\,{}^\circ\text{C}$. Ice taken from the freezer at $-20\,{}^\circ\text{C}$ is to be added to the water. The amount of ice is chosen so that the ice melts exactly completely and the temperature of the mixture becomes $0\,{}^\circ\text{C}$. How many grams of ice are needed? Give the answer in grams.

An insulated container holds $0.200\,\text{kg}$ of water at $15.0\,{}^\circ\text{C}$. $0.300\,\text{kg}$ of ice at $-10.0\,{}^\circ\text{C}$ is added to the water. How many grams of ice are left in the container when thermal equilibrium has been reached? First check whether all the ice melts. Give the answer in grams.

An insulated container holds $0.100\,\text{kg}$ of water at $10.0\,{}^\circ\text{C}$. $0.500\,\text{kg}$ of ice at $-40.0\,{}^\circ\text{C}$ is added to the water. What is the temperature of the contents of the container when thermal equilibrium has been reached? First work out whether all the water freezes. Give the answer in degrees Celsius.
